This protein is identified as a target of both 3-Epidehydrotumulosic Acid and Diffutidin, which are compounds that may interact with Bipinnatone A. The scores from the three paths indicate a consistent level of confidence in the relationship, with the highest scores (0.6029) from Path 1 and 2, and a slightly lower score (0.5667) from Path 3. The evidence suggests that Bipinnatone A may act as a modulator of the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 3, which in turn may influence the activity of Methionine aminopeptidase 2. The mechanism is not fully elucidated, but the shared target of multiple compounds implies a possible regulatory pathway. The evidence supports a plausible biological interaction, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be determined.
